function: Joint transmit beamforming at the multi-antenna CRBS and active-RIS reflection coefficients (gain and phase) to maximize the minimum weighted SINR of multicast users (p. 1, 7).
system: Active RIS of M=8-24 units (uniform planar array); CRBS with N=8 antennas; single-antenna SUs and PUs (Ks=4, Kp=2, G=2); band not stated (p. 3, 10).
method: Reinforcement learning with DDPG and TD3 actor-critic agents at the CRBS; MDP with action {W, phi} and segmented reward with penalty terms; experience replay (p. 7-9).
data_channel: Simulated Rician channels (factor 5), log-distance path loss; "channel model is based on LTE [42]" (3GPP TR 36.873); fixed CRBS and RIS, random user positions (p. 10).
test_conditions: Same simulated environment throughout; results swept over CRBS power 20-40 dBm, M=8-24 and gain 10-50, with no trained model applied to an unseen scenario (p. 11-12).
baselines: Non-learned: own AO (SCA/PCCP) with active RIS, AO with passive RIS, AO with no RIS. Learned: only DDPG vs TD3, both proposed here (p. 3, 12).
metrics: Average weighted minimum SINR (dB) of the secondary users versus transmit power, RIS size and gain; average reward versus steps (p. 11-12).
complexity: Big-O orders only: AO subproblems o_W, o_Theta (p. 9); DDPG and TD3 application and training complexity in layer sizes (p. 10); no runtime or FLOPs.
q1_support: p. 10: "The channel model is based on LTE [42]". [42] is 3GPP TR 36.873 (3D channel model for LTE, p. 14), not TR 38.901; the Rice factor 5 and the path loss are set by the authors.
q2_support: p. 11: "units varies in the range of [8, 24] with an interval of 4". Only sweeps of CRBS power, RIS size and gain; no trained model is tested on another scenario and no fine-tuning or transfer is reported.
q3_support: p. 3: "(DDPG)-based and twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3)-based algorithms are proposed". Both learned curves are the paper's own algorithms; the other baselines are non-learned AO (p. 11); no earlier learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 10: "complexity for the DDPG algorithm is given by". Sec. V gives big-O orders for AO (p. 9) and for DDPG and TD3 application and training (p. 10); no runtime or FLOPs.
q5_support: p. 10: "The Rice factor is set as 5". Channels come from the authors' simulator; no code or data link is given, and the only URL is the CVX tool (p. 14).
notes: Included, area 3: DRL (DDPG, TD3) designs CRBS beamforming and active-RIS reflection jointly. Checks 1-7 pass (multi-antenna CRBS, N=8, p. 3 and 10; results p. 11-12). q1 is borderline: the paper says it is based on LTE [42], i.e. 3GPP TR 36.873 (p. 14), another standardized model than TR 38.901, with Rician K=5 and a custom path loss; reviewer to confirm. q3 is borderline: DDPG and TD3 are both proposed (p. 3, 9) and TD3 only adds twin critics, so I treated DDPG as a variant; it would be 1 if the reviewer counts DDPG as a standard algorithm applied to the same problem. q2 is 0: the state size depends on M (p. 7), which suggests a new agent per setting, but this is not stated. Whole paper read, with Table I and Figs. 2-7 opened as images.
